title: Got a Diwali Bonus? Five Ways to Strengthen Your Finances
excerpt: Emergency savings first, high-interest dues second, then investing, planned home repairs and a capped celebration budget — how to give a festive bonus a job before it is spent.
body:
• Before festive spending, give the bonus a job: Outlook Money's five-way split is emergency savings, clearing pending dues, investing for future goals, planned home repairs, and a capped celebration budget.
  • Keep part of the bonus in an emergency fund covering at least three months of essential expenses, Outlook Money advises; Bajaj Finserv puts the ideal range at three to six months of living expenses, held separately from everyday spending.
  • Use part of the bonus to clear credit card bills and high-interest loans first — Bajaj Finserv notes that paying down such debt can also lower your credit utilisation ratio.
  • For the reader: decide the split before you shop — Bajaj Finserv's FAQ suggests a 50/30/20 fallback of 50% for immediate needs, 30% for long-term goals and 20% for personal use if you are unsure.

A Diwali bonus is extra money at the most expensive-feeling time of the year. Outlook Money frames the choice plainly: it is tempting to spend it all during the festive season, but the bonus can also be made to strengthen your finances while you still enjoy Diwali. Its five ways, reinforced by Bajaj Finserv's guide to using a Diwali bonus, are set out below in the order that protects you first.

1. Put some money aside first

Unexpected expenses can come up at any time, Outlook Money notes. It advises keeping part of the bonus in an emergency fund to cover at least three months of essential expenses. Bajaj Finserv puts the ideal emergency fund at three to six months of living expenses, held in a bank account separate from your primary spending account so you do not dip into it for regular expenses. If you already have a fund, the bonus can give it a substantial boost.

2. Clear pending dues before a big purchase

Before planning a big festive purchase, check credit card bills and outstanding loans, Outlook Money advises. Using the bonus to clear high-interest debt saves money on future interest payments. Bajaj Finserv makes the same point: clearing outstanding credit card balances and personal loans frees up money for more productive uses, and paying down card debt can increase a credit score by bringing down the credit utilisation ratio.

3. Invest for the future goals you actually have

Part of the bonus can work towards bigger goals such as retirement or a child's education, Outlook Money says, with investments chosen based on your goals, risk tolerance and time horizon. Bajaj Finserv adds two practical routes: diversify into new options that align with your goals and risk tolerance, or increase allocation in investments you already hold — which, it notes, can capitalise on compounding in long-term, retirement-focused investments and systematic investment plans (SIPs), while keeping your original asset allocation intact.

4. Take care of home repairs — planned, not improvised

If you want your home ready for Diwali, Outlook Money suggests using some of the bonus for necessary repairs or improvements, planning the costs beforehand and leaving room for unexpected expenses. Bajaj Finserv notes home improvements can indirectly support financial health by increasing a property's value, and advises focusing on areas with the best return — and on work done at the right time, before disrepair becomes more expensive to fix.

5. Enjoy Diwali, on a budget you set first

You do not have to choose between celebrating and saving, Outlook Money says: set aside a budget for gifts, shopping and festivities, then use what is left for debt repayment or investments. Bajaj Finserv's guidance for readers who are unsure how to split the bonus is a 50/30/20 rule — 50% for immediate needs, 30% for long-term goals and 20% for personal use. Outlook Money's closing advice is the discipline underneath all five steps: before spending, take a quick look at your savings, debts and upcoming expenses, and give the bonus a purpose first.

Two further uses Bajaj Finserv lists are worth checking while the money is in hand: reviewing life, health, home and auto insurance to see whether coverage is still sufficient, and investing in your own skills — a course that upgrades career prospects and earning potential. Neither replaces the five steps above; both are ways to stop a one-off payment leaking away without a trace.
